coordinates.note: ESTIMATED from video. Accuracy depends on the field registration — see the 'registration' block if present. These are not exact positions.
coordinates.units: yards; x downfield 0-120 with the offense attacking +x, y across 0-53.3

orientation.note: o is body orientation, dir is direction of travel; they are different and must not be derived from each other. o_source on every row says how that value was arrived at.

gaze.note: Where a player was LOOKING is not measured by anything, in this or any public football dataset. No such column exists here. The closest available signal is interactions.ball_in_view, which is inferred from body orientation and marked as inferred on every record.

jerseys.method: Apple Vision; agreement across at least three independent frames
jerseys.note: OCR estimates; conflicting or unreadable jerseys remain unknown.

ball.flight_projection: ground-plane projection of image sightings; altitude is not recovered
ball.note: A football in a wide broadcast shot is a few pixels and is behind somebody most of the play. Read measured_fraction AND travelled_yards before trusting any possession, passer or throw derived from this: a high detection rate on a static object is a confident wrong answer, and the generic sports-ball class finds broadcast graphics.

identity.method: automatic detector-seeded SAM 2 with backward crossing and single-player reacquisition checks

backwardChecks.reason: later observations do not match the earlier identity seam

observationChecks.method: exclusive detector/SAM association with immutable kit and motion gates

roleCheck.method: local uniform roles before roster seeding

identity.note: Fixed IDs and teams persist. Hidden poses are absent from observation data and filled explicitly for replay; backward corrections require a matching earlier identity seam.

replayStability.method: fixed roster; future-bracketed interpolation; damped coast and hold; smoothed display positions
replayStability.note: All roster actors persist. Missing positions are display estimates, not new observations. Original samples are retained in observation.

analysisBlockers: which side has the ball could not be established. With no ball track and no pre-snap frames there is nothing to decide it on — check that the clip's window opens before the snap, and that snap_frame is the snap rather than the first frame of the window.

the ball was never actually seen: 28% of samples are attributed to whoever was carrying it, not detected. That places the ball to about a yard while it is being carried, so the track will draw a run correctly and can be exported — but a carried ball has no position while it is in the air, so the throw and the arrival cannot be located and a pass review keyed on this would be confident and meaningless. For a run this blocker is the only thing standing between the clip and a review; for a pass, a ball detector that clears 25% is needed.

trackingQuality.identity: automatic detector-seeded SAM 2 with backward crossing and single-player reacquisition checks

roleCheck.method: local uniform roles before roster seeding

notes: Same-kit crossings may switch identities; roster size does not establish identity accuracy.
Unobserved players retain estimated replay positions. Analysis uses original observations; separation estimates may miss off-camera defenders.
Unidentified positions can cause linemen to be treated as possible receivers.
